items.label: FIGURE 2.3
items.title: There has been considerable progress in reducing the Global Prosperity Gap since 1990
items.content: The chart is a line chart showing the Global Prosperity Gap from 1990 to 2024. The y-axis represents the Global Prosperity Gap, ranging from 0 to 12. The x-axis represents years from 1990 to 2024. The trend shows a steady decline in the gap over time, starting at approximately 10.9 in 1990 and reaching approximately 5.0 in 2024. There are two visible increases: one between 1997 and 1998 (Asian financial crisis) and one between 2019 and 2020 (COVID-19 pandemic). The line from 2023 to 2024 is dashed, indicating projections. Source: World Bank, Poverty and Inequality Platform (version September 2024), https://pip.worldbank.org. Note: The estimates in 2023 and 2024 are projected. The prosperity threshold is set at $25 per person per day in 2017 purchasing power parity dollars.
